title: Converting a zero-error partial verifier to RP
statement: Let $E$ be a verifier model with two closure properties: it can efficiently turn an efficient partial verifier into the Boolean test that its output equals a fixed bit, and it can efficiently take the specified disjunction of polynomially many tests on disjoint random-tape blocks. Suppose $M$ is efficient, $a,k$ are natural numbers, $L'$ is a language, and $b$ is a bit. For each $x\in L'$, assume that on every random tape of length $a(|x|+1)^k$, $M$ never outputs the bit opposite to $b$ and the probability it outputs no answer is at most $1/2$; for each $x\notin L'$, assume that on every such tape it never outputs $b$. Then $L'$ has an efficient one-sided randomized verifier in $E$, accepting members with probability at least $2/3$ and rejecting nonmembers with certainty.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is closed under efficiently testing whether a verifier's output equals a fixed bit.
$E$ is closed under the specified polynomially many-test disjunction construction.
$a,k$ are natural numbers specifying random-string length $a(|x|+1)^k$.
$L'$ is a language of bit strings.
On each member, every random string avoids outputting $!b$, and the no-answer probability is at most $1/2$.
On each nonmember, every random string avoids outputting $b$.
